narrative.northStar: The Ember in the Dark Room
narrative.overview:
The system behaves like a single warm light in an unlit room. The ground is near-black with red in it, not neutral grey, and every accent sits on one warm ramp running from deep rust through ember orange to pale gold. Colour is not decoration here: it is the signal that something is alive, permitted, or currently selected.

The product's own metaphor drives the visual one. A company brain is a tree that grows from a root, and the marketing surface renders that literally as a glowing tree drawn limb by limb as the reader scrolls. The authenticated surface then deliberately turns the light down: the same palette, the same faces, but colour withdrawn to actions, selection and state.

The result is two registers of one world. Marketing is allowed to be scenic. The app is restrained. The serif crosses that border exactly once per screen, on the page title, and never touches a label, a control or a value.
keyCharacteristics: One warm ramp; no cool hue anywhere in the system.
Light-as-material: glow means emission, not depth. Depth is tonal.
Two registers, one palette: scenic marketing, restrained product.
Text tints are the foreground at lower opacity, never grey.
Motion earns its place once per surface, then stops.

rules.name: The One Ramp Rule
rules.body: Every colour in the system is a step on the rust to ember to gold ramp, plus the two semantic signals. There is no blue, no violet, no grey. A proposed colour that cannot be placed on that ramp does not belong to this system.

rules.name: The Tinted Text Rule
rules.body: Secondary and tertiary text is the cream foreground at reduced opacity, never a grey. The alpha floor is .52; below that, 4.5:1 against the ground gives out.

rules.name: The Semantic Distance Rule
rules.body: Only two semantic colours exist, and both are deliberately far enough from the accent that a status pill can never be mistaken for a button.

rules.name: The One Serif Per Screen Rule
rules.body: The display serif appears once on an authenticated screen, as its title. A serif label, a serif button, or a serif value is always wrong.

rules.name: The -0.02em Floor Rule
rules.body: Display tracking never goes tighter than -0.02em. The system previously ran -0.059em at 118px and the letterforms collided.

rules.name: The 13px Floor Rule
rules.body: No real text renders below 0.8125rem. Metadata that will not fit at that size is metadata the screen does not need.

rules.name: The Glow-Is-Light Rule
rules.body: A zero-offset coloured shadow is only permitted on an element that is supposed to be emitting light. Everything else uses tone and a hairline. A glowing card is a category error.

rules: Disabled is a colour, not a transparency: fading a control fades its text and its ground together. Disabled primary is rgba(255,180,90,.2) under rgba(255,245,229,.75); every other disabled control keeps its ground and drops its text to --on-night-subtle. Nothing disabled falls below 5:1.
No low-opacity warm radial over a working surface. It reads as haze rather than light, and a contrast checker reading through it reported 2:1 for text that measures 17.7:1.
dos: Do place every new colour on the rust to ember to gold ramp, or justify it as one of the two semantic signals.
Do convey depth with the three ground tones and a hairline.
Do tint secondary text from the cream foreground, never toward grey, and never below .52 alpha.
Do reset background: transparent on any button base class.
Do give every interactive element hover, focus-visible, active, disabled and busy before shipping it.
Do keep one authored motion moment per surface and use cubic-bezier(.16, 1, .3, 1) at 200-300ms for everything else.
donts: Don't put an eyebrow or kicker label above a heading. The heading carries its own weight.
Don't number sections (01 / 02 / 03) unless the sequence itself is information the reader needs.
Don't use monospace as a costume for technical. It is for keys, commands and code.
Don't build a page out of same-size cards of dot plus heading plus text.
Don't stand a Unicode glyph in for an icon. Icons are drawn SVG at a single 1.5 stroke.
Don't ramp a gradient from the night ground to the daylight cream. Every such interpolation passes through mud.
Don't animate padding, width, height or margin. Transform and opacity only.
Don't let the display serif touch a label, a control, or a value.
